title: Health and Safety Advisor
description: Let’s Talk About the Role At Resmed, the health and safety of our people is fundamental to how we work. We are looking for a Health & Safety Advisor who is passionate about creating safer workplaces and enjoys working alongside leaders and teams to turn good safety practices into everyday habits. In this role, you will be a trusted Health & Safety partner across our Australian operations, providing practical advice, strengthening our safety systems and helping leaders and teams build a proactive safety culture where everyone takes ownership of safety. This is more than a compliance role. You will spend time where the work happens – partnering with leaders and employees, understanding how work is performed, solving practical safety challenges and identifying opportunities to continuously improve the way we work. If you enjoy combining technical Health & Safety expertise with coaching, problem-solving and genuine partnership, this is an opportunity to make a visible impact on the safety and experience of our people. Responsibilities: Be a trusted Health & Safety partner You will work closely with leaders and employees to make Health & Safety practical, accessible and part of everyday decision-making. You will: Provide timely and practical Health & Safety advice to leaders, employees and key stakeholders. Interpret WHS legislation, standards and internal requirements and translate them into practical workplace solutions. Coach leaders to understand and confidently fulfil their Health & Safety responsibilities. Build strong relationships across manufacturing, operational and corporate teams. Support effective consultation and engagement with employees, Health & Safety Representatives and Health & Safety Committees. Lead and embed a proactive safety culture by partnering with leaders and teams to strengthen safety ownership, accountability and everyday safe behaviours. Foster an environment where employees feel confident to speak up about safety, proactively identify and report risks, and contribute ideas that improve workplace safety. Strengthen risk management & prevention A key focus of the role is helping us identify risks early and prevent incidents before they occur. You will: Facilitate and support workplace risk assessments, hazard identification and implementation of effective controls. Partner with teams to review existing controls and identify opportunities to strengthen them. Maintain and support effective management of Health & Safety risk registers. Analyse hazards, incidents, near misses and safety observations to identify trends and emerging risks. Translate insights into practical preventative actions and improvement initiatives. Provide Health & Safety input into workplace changes, new equipment, processes and projects. Support ergonomic and workplace design risk assessments from a preventative and systems perspective. Support incident investigation & continuous improvement When incidents occur, you will help the organisation learn from them and prevent recurrence. You will: Support the timely reporting, assessment and investigation of workplace incidents and near misses. Facilitate effective incident investigations and root cause analysis. Partner with leaders to develop practical corrective and preventative actions. Monitor actions through to completion and evaluate whether controls have been effective. Identify recurring themes and use insights to shape broader Health & Safety improvement priorities. Support the development and delivery of Health & Safety improvement plans, initiatives and projects. Build Health & Safety capability Great safety outcomes come from capable and confident leaders and teams. You will: Develop and deliver engaging Health & Safety training, education and awareness programs. Provide ongoing coaching to leaders and employees on safe work practices and risk management. Support Health & Safety inductions and other required safety training. Identify capability gaps and recommend practical ways to strengthen safety knowledge and behaviours. Develop clear and engaging Health & Safety communications, tools and resources. Support safety campaigns and initiatives that encourage active employee participation. Strengthen our Health & Safety systems You will help ensure our Health & Safety systems remain effective, contemporary and easy for our people to use. You will: Support the development, implementation and continuous improvement of Health & Safety policies, procedures and safe systems of work. Help maintain and strengthen our Health & Safety Management System. Support internal and external Health & Safety audits, inspections and assurance activities. Monitor corrective actions, audit findings and improvement commitments through to closure. Maintain accurate Health & Safety documentation, records and reporting. Monitor Health & Safety performance indicators and provide meaningful insights to leaders. Support compliance with applicable WHS legislation, regulatory requirements and Resmed standards. Let’s Talk About You You are a practical and collaborative Health & Safety professional who enjoys being close to the business and making safety work in the real world. You are comfortable moving between the shop floor and leadership conversations – whether that means facilitating a risk assessment, investigating an incident, coaching a leader or using data to identify where we can do better. You bring curiosity and sound judgement. Rather than simply pointing to a policy or requirement, you seek to understand the work, engage the people closest to it and find solutions that are both safe and practical. You will bring: Demonstrated experience in a Health & Safety, WHS role. Sound knowledge of Australian WHS legislation, regulations and contemporary Health & Safety practices. Experience undertaking risk assessments, incident investigations and corrective action management. The ability to interpret Health & Safety requirements and translate them into practical workplace solutions. Strong consultation, coaching and influencing skills. Confidence partnering with leaders and employees at different levels of an organisation. Strong problem-solving skills and a proactive, prevention-focused mindset. The ability to analyse safety information and trends and translate insights into meaningful action. Strong organisational and documentation skills. The ability to work independently while collaborating effectively across a broader team. Qualifications and Experience Essential A relevant qualification in Work Health & Safety, Health & Safety, Risk Management or a related discipline. Demonstrated experience working in a Health & Safety advisory role. Practical experience with workplace risk assessment, incident investigation and Health & Safety management systems. Working knowledge of Australian WHS legislation and regulatory requirements. Strong stakeholder engagement, consultation and communication skills. We'd Also Love to See Experience within manufacturing, medical devices, healthcare, engineering or another highly regulated environment . Experience working with ISO 45001 or another recognised Health & Safety management system. Formal incident investigation or root cause analysis training. Experience supporting Health & Safety audits and regulatory interactions. Experience delivering Health & Safety training and coaching leaders. Exposure to ergonomics, manual handling, machinery safety, hazardous substances or contractor safety. Experience supporting organisational change, new equipment, facility or process risk assessments. Where a culture driven by excellence helps you not only meet your goals, but also create new ones. We focus on creating a diverse and inclusive culture, encouraging individual expression in the workplace and thrive on the innovative ideas this generates. title: Change and Capability Partner- Manufacturing Excellence Program
description: Change & Capability Partner – Manufacturing Excellence Program IN ONE LINE The execution engine for the people side of MEP — landing the change plan, the communications and the capability rollout with rhythm and finesse, using the standards and pathways set by the People Team Centre of Excellence. ROLE PURPOSE This role makes the MEP change land. It takes the agreed change and capability strategy and turns it into the practical work — the plan, the calendar, the communications, the training rollout, the pulse checks and the follow-through — across every site, wave and squad in the programme. It is a Change and Capability Partner role which requires very thorough executional approach. Strategy, standards and organisation design decisions sit with the Director, People Business Partnering and the People Team Centre of Excellence. This role brings the discipline, the materials and the rhythm that turn those decisions into adoption on the floor. WORKING WITH THE PEOPLE TEAM The People Team is the Centre of Excellence. It sets the global standards for talent and development, owns the capability frameworks and designs the learning pathways. This role deploys them inside MEP — it does not rebuild them. Everything runs through the Director, People Business Partnering and the People Business Partners, and everything learned along the way goes back into the CoE. PEOPLE TEAM — CENTRE OF EXCELLENCE OWNS CHANGE & CAPABILITY PARTNER EXECUTES Global standards for talent, development and capability — the frameworks, levels and definitions Applies those standards inside MEP; never creates a parallel framework Design and ownership of learning pathways and curricula Schedules, deploys and tracks those pathways across sites, waves and squads Capability architecture, assessment methodology and proficiency definitions Runs the assessment logistics, collects the data, reports the results back to the CoE Organisation design, role architecture and people strategy decisions Provides impact evidence and implementation support; does not set direction WHAT YOU WILL DO 1 Run the change plan and its rhythm Turn the agreed change strategy into a working execution plan across phases, sites, waves and squads. Keep the milestone tracker, communication calendar, engagement plan and training schedule current and connected to the wider MEP delivery plan. Hold the cadence — the routines, check-ins, reviews and follow-ups that keep change moving alongside technical delivery. Track actions, risks and dependencies, and prepare short, honest updates for programme leadership and the Director, People Business Partnering. 2 Craft and land the narrative Draft the MEP change materials: case for change, leader cascade packs, manager toolkits, FAQs, town hall content, intranet updates and progress notes. Execute the communications plan across the right mediums for each audience — floor, line, site and leadership. Work with Communications and the People Business Partners so messaging stays consistent with the approved narrative. Keep the story current as the programme moves, so people always know what is changing and what it means for them. 3 Engage the stakeholders Maintain stakeholder maps and impact views across leaders, site teams, engineers, technicians, operators and delivery partners. Coordinate workshops, leader briefings, manager cascades, champion routines and go-and-see activity. Surface resistance, change fatigue and adoption barriers early, with practical options rather than just observations. 4 Deploy capability using People Team pathways Schedule and deploy the learning pathways designed by the People Team CoE — train-the-trainer, super-user routines and role-based sessions. Run capability assessment logistics and collect the data; the methodology and proficiency definitions stay with the CoE. Track participation, proficiency and post-training support needs so capability is measured beyond attendance. Feed findings and site realities back to the People Team so pathways improve for the next wave. 5 Take the pulse and reinforce Run pulse surveys, listening loops and manager routine checks at a steady beat through the transformation. Maintain readiness and adoption dashboards that make status, barriers and support needs visible to programme leadership. Watch whether new processes, systems and routines are actually being embedded — and act where reinforcement is needed. Support hypercare and the handover to business as usual after each go-live. Capture lessons into reusable playbooks and templates, and hand them back to the People Team CoE. WHAT YOU WILL DELIVER Change and capability execution plan, milestone tracker and communication calendar. Stakeholder map, engagement plan and feedback log. Leader cascade materials, manager toolkits, FAQs and approved communications content. Training deployment schedule, participation and proficiency tracking — against CoE pathways. Readiness and adoption dashboards, pulse survey insights and reinforcement actions. Reusable MEP change playbook, handed back to the People Team Centre of Excellence. HOW SUCCESS IS MEASURED Change deliverables land on the agreed milestones and stay integrated with the MEP delivery plan. Leaders and managers have clear, current materials to explain the change and what it asks of their teams. Adoption risks, capability gaps and readiness issues surface early — with options attached. Training deployment is tracked to proficiency, not attendance, and reported back to the CoE. Pulse and adoption data show whether new ways of working are being embedded, wave by wave. Standards and pathways are applied consistently — no parallel frameworks are created inside MEP. The People Team CoE ends the programme with better playbooks than it started with. WHAT YOU BRING 5+ years in change management, capability deployment, learning rollout, operational excellence or complex programme execution. Proven delivery of change and capability plans across multi-site, cross-functional environments. Manufacturing, supply chain, engineering, lean, automation or MES / digital adoption experience — strongly preferred. Strong execution discipline: planning, dependency management, action tracking and clear reporting. Excellent writing — the ability to draft materials that leaders, managers and frontline teams actually use. Credibility with senior leaders and shop-floor teams alike, and comfort working at pace with ambiguity. Change certification (Prosci / ADKAR or similar) and regulated or medical device manufacturing experience are advantageous. HOW YOU WILL WORK Embedded in the MEP core team, reporting to the Senior Director, Manufacturing Excellence Programme. Partnered closely with the Director, People Business Partnering and the People Business Partners — the route into the Centre of Excellence.
